newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Capral says smelting earnings lag.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Capral says smelting earnings lag.

text.p: Capral Aluminium Ltd said on Tuesday its earnings from smelting and trading declined to A$28.6 million in 1996 from A$96.6 million in 1995 due to lower sales prices for aluminium and increasing costs of some raw materials
The full impact was partially offset by an increase in production of primary aluminium to 150,000 tonnes in 1996 from 142,000 tonnes in 1995, Capral said.
Capral earlier on Tuesday reported a net profit of A$29.42 million for 1996, down from A$60.32 million in 1995.
Capral, formerly Alcan Australia Ltd, operates the Kurri Kurri smelter in New South Wales.
Downstream business earnings increased to 40 percent to A$41 million in 1996, the company said.

"The increase largely reflects the successful absorption into the group of the businesses acquired from Comalco Ltd in December 1995 and of continuing streamlining and rationalisation, particularly in the extrusion and distribution businesses," Capral said.
Downstream markets remained subdued and were subject to strong competitive forces, Capral said.
Sales of fabricated products increased to 96,000 tonnes in 1996 from 77,000 tonnes in 1995, it said.
The decline in net profit was caused by a 16 percent drop in the average London Metal Exchange aluminium price to US$1,537 a tonne in 1996 from US$1,833 in 1996, Capral said.
In Australian dollar terms, the decline was more severe at 21 percent, Capral noted.
"At the same time world markets have seen an increasing level of competition and the added value metal premiums have declined," the company said.
Total sales declined by four percent to A$796 million while export sales dropped 22 percent to A$166 million, largely due to lower prices, the company said.
The export shortfall was only partially offset by an increase in domestic sales to A$630 million from A$617 million, Capral said.
Capral said its balance sheet was strong and benefited from a reduction in stocks and debtors by nearly A$31 million in the year.
"The net debt-to-equity ratio has reduced from 25 percent in 1995 to 21 percent (in 1996) and leaves the company in a strong position for further expansion," Capral said.
Capral, formerly Alcan Australia Ltd, operates the Kurri Kurri smelter in New South Wales state.
